{{Short description|British chemist}}
'''Leslie Bretherick''' (1926&ndash;2003) was a [[chemist]] and an “internationally recognized authority on [[laboratory safety]]”<ref name=Renfrew88>{{cite journal | last1 = Renfrew | first1 = M | year = 1988 | title =  Chemical demonstrations: A sourcebook for teachers, volume 2 (Summerlin, Lee R.; Borgford, Christie L.; Ealy, Julie B.)| doi = 10.1021/ed065pA171 | journal = Journal of Chemical Education | volume = 65 | issue = 6| page = A171 }}</ref> especially remembered for writing the book which became ''[[Bretherick's Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards]]'', an indexed guide to published data on dangerous chemical reactions.  An obituary said “His contributions  have improved the lives of countless millions, and I will aver, have saved the lives of thousands”.<ref name=Obituary>{{cite journal | last1 = Young | first1 = Jay | year = 2003 | title =  Obituary| doi = 10.1016/S1074-9098(03)00066-2 | journal = Chemical Health and Safety | volume = 10 | issue = 4| page = 46 }}</ref>

==Life==
Bretherick was born in 1926 <ref name=birth>Publishers and libraries author dates</ref> and received a BSc from the [[University of Liverpool]] in 1946<ref name=bio>{{cite journal | last1 = Bretherick | first1 = L | year = 1979 | title =  Reactive chemical hazards: Their causes and prevention| doi = 10.1021/ed056pA57 | journal = Journal of Chemical Education | volume = 56 | issue = 2| page = A57 }}</ref>  He worked for [[May & Baker]] from 1945 to 1960,<ref name=Renfrew88/> where a personal injury and a near-miss provoked his lifelong interest in the prevention of chemical accidents.<ref name=Barker>{{cite journal | last1 = Barker | first1 = P.E. | last2 = Bretherick | first2 = L. | last3 = Kay | first3 = F.A.A. | year = 1993 | title = Problems and Solutions in the Development of Hard and Soft Versions of a Chemical Reaction Hazards Database | doi = 10.1021/ci00012a001 | journal = J. Chem. Inf. Comput. Sci. | volume = 33 | issue = | pages = 184–192 }}</ref> He then had two years in chemical production at L. Light & Co before moving to [[BP]] Research Centre, [[Sunbury-on-Thames]], in 1962 where he stayed till his early retirement in 1982.<ref name=Renfrew88/>
It was there that he produced his [[magnum opus]], nearly 1000 pages summarizing published literature on chemical accidents and dangerous reactions, organised by individual compound in 1975.<ref>Bretherick, L. (1975) ''Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards'' Butterworths (London)</ref>  A second edition followed in 1979. As well as corrections and additional reactions, this contained a new section dealing with groups of compounds and some other matters. A third edition followed in 1985, Bretherick having retired in 1982 in order to work full-time on the project.<ref name=third>Preface to the Third Edition, 1985</ref><ref name=Barker/> In the preface to the 4th edition (1989) he announced that his eyesight was failing.<ref name=Fourth>Preface to the Fourth Edition, 1989</ref>  As a result, he did not contribute new material to further editions, which was done by others.  The fourth edition onwards were titled ''Bretherick’s Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards''.

In 1988, Bretherick received the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) Chemical Health and Safety Award for his outstanding contributions in the field of chemical health and safety.<ref name = ACS>[http://dchas.org/howard-fawcett-chemical-health-and-safety-award/ ACS] Howard Fawcett Chemical Health and Safety Award</ref><ref name=RenfrewAward>{{cite journal | last1 = Renfrew | first1 = M | year = 1990 | title =  Chemical laboratory safety: The academic anomaly| doi = 10.1021/ed067pA12 | journal = Journal of Chemical Education | volume = 67 | issue = 1| page = A12 }}</ref>

He was a [[Chartered Chemist]] and Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC).  He also edited a RSC handbook on chemical laboratory hazards,<ref name=HCBbk>Bretherick L., (ed) (1981) ''Hazards in the Chemical Laboratory 3rd ed'' Royal Society of Chemistry (London)</ref> as well as numerous articles on chemical safety.  He was selected as one of the RSC’s “175 Faces of Chemistry”<ref name=Faces>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/leslie-bretherick-cchem-frsc|title= 175 Faces of Chemistry - Leslie Bretherick FRSC|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121165653/http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/leslie-bretherick-cchem-frsc|archivedate=21 November 2016}}</ref> noting that his achievements were made despite poor eyesight (and eventual near blindness) and a [[stammering|stammer]] (he was an active member of the [[British Stammering Association]]).<ref name=Faces/>  He was a member of the [[Macular Society|Macular Disease Society]].<ref name=photo>{{cite journal |last1=Bretherick |first1=Leslie |date=1991 |title=Photography for the visually impaired |url= |journal=The British Journal of Visual Impairment |volume=9 |issue= 3|page=109 |doi= 10.1177/026461969100900326|access-date= }}</ref>

He died in April 2003, survived by his wife, Margaret.<ref name=Faces/>
